sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A densely branched, deciduous, spineless shrub native across much of Europe and into western Asia. It bears lobed leaves and upright greenish-yellow flower clusters; male and female flowers are on separate plants. Mature height and spread are commonly about 1–2 m, though clipped hedges are often kept lower.

sections.title: Fruit and use
sections.text: Female plants can produce small red berries, about 7 mm across, if pollinated. They are edible but described as bland or less palatable than redcurrants; the sources consulted do not report a specific toxicity.
